full_judgment: 2. The predecessor of the plaintiff-landlords and the predecessor of the defendant tenant entered into two lease agreements in respect of the suit premises on 12-1-1988 upon creating a monthly tenancy in the suit premises which were, subsequently, renewed from time to time on mutual consent. Lastly, on 22-1-1995 the predecessor of the plaintiff-landlords and the present defendant-appellant- tenant entered into two agreements for monthly tenancy in respect of the same for a period of two years ending on 31-12-1996 at a monthly rent of Taka 12,000 for the building situated therein and Taka 40,000 for the vacant place of the suit premises in total Taka 52,000 to be paid by the first week of every month. In the said agreement it was contemplated that the agreement would expire on 31-12- 1996 determining the landlord tenant relationship and the same will not be extended or renewed any further under any circumstances. It was also contended that the 2nd party tenant would hand over the vacant possession of the suit premises to the landlords on 1-1-1997 without fail upon removing all structures constructed by the tenant therein. It was further agreed by the tenant that in case he fails to handover the vacant possession of the suit premises to the landlords after 31-12-1996 then the tenant would pay Taka 1,000 for each agreement i.e. Taka 2,000 for each day's possession of the same. He further agreed that all the temporary structures constructed in the suit premises will be removed immediately on the expiry of the said agreements. According to one of the clauses of the said agreements the tenant deposited Taka 1,60,000, equivalent to four month's rent for the vacant space in one deed and Taka 48,000, equivalent to four month's rent for the building in another deed as security which would not be adjusted with the rent rather at the time of handing over possession, after the expiry of the tenancy period the entire security money would be refunded to the tenant. The said agreements also contended that at the time of handing over possession of the suit premises the tenant would hand over the receipts of all the paid up utility bills for Electricity, Gas, WASA, Telephone etc. in full which he consumed, to the landlord and thereby handover the possession of the suit premises without any encumbrances. But it is alleged by the plaintiff landlords that the defendant tenant defaulted in paying rent of the suit premises for the month of December 1996 when he paid the same on the 8th of December as such he became a defaulter and is liable to be evicted from the suit premises. It is further alleged that the defendant tenant did not pay the rent for the month of August 2003 till date nor he handover the possession of the same to the plaintiff landlords upon removing the unauthorized structures constructed thereon after the expiry of the tenancy on 31-12-1996 rather inspite of repeated intimations to vacant the suit premises as per agreement he continued to possess the same without paying rent and compensation to the plaintiff landlord. As such the plaintiff landlord, on 2-8-2003, issued a notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act by registered post with A/D upon the defendant tenant which has been duly received by the defendant tenant on 6-8-2003. But the defendant tenant did not comply with the requests/directions made in the legal notice. As such the plaintiff landlord filed the present suit on 6-9-2003 for ejectment of the monthly tenant; for payment of the outstanding rent of Taka 49,28,000 for the suit premises from 1-1-1997 till September 2003 at the rate of Taka 2000 per day along with direction upon the defendant tenant to pay the utility costs which may be due and remove the unauthorized constructions made therein, for Khas possession in case the defendant after the decree, does not makeover the possession of the suit premises to the plaintiffs.
